changes.comment: Code organization refactor stage 6b item 6 (R10): rewrote TeamClosing's dissolve/close sequence. TeamClosingDeps drops the leader()/closeLeaderForDissolve() callback pair; dissolve(input, leader), abandonCreation(input, leader), and stopForHost(leader) now all take the TeamLeader as a plain AgentService | null value, read once by TeamService (its own leader_ field) at each call site instead of asked for through a callback. stopChildRuntimesForDissolve and the child-stopping half of stopRuntimesForDissolve are unified as stopChildrenForDissolve() and stopAllForDissolve(leader), both still built on the one shared, non-throwing stopChildRuntimes(failures) helper so a member-stop failure and a leader-stop failure still aggregate into one thrown error exactly as today; closeResources (now closeChildren) drops its own redundant repeat of workflows.closeAdmission()/stopAll() and scheduler.stop() -- both were already covered, idempotently, by stopAllForDissolve immediately before it, so the repeat inside closeResources answered nothing new. abandonCreation's adoptDurableLeader callback is removed: TeamService.createNew's own catch adopts an orphaned durable leader itself, before calling abandonCreation, and passes the result as the leader argument; a failure during that adoption attempt is now logged rather than folded into the thrown AggregateError alongside the original creation-failure cause. The number, order, and gating of every worktree assessment, the dissolve refusal contract, the dissolve receipt shape, and team.closed timing are unchanged. TeamService forgets this.leader_ (checked once, after closing.dissolve() settles) whenever the new AgentService.isSafeToForget() is true, not only once AgentService.isRetired() confirms the close's own durable write also landed: a leader whose close() fully released runtime authority (stopRuntime() succeeded) but whose identity write then failed is still forgotten and rebuilt fresh from disk on next use, matching the pre-refactor unconditional pre-close null. isSafeToForget() stays false for the different case of an unproven runtime termination (a failed start whose own rollback stop could not prove the native runtime dead), because that runtime might still be alive and must not be silently forgotten. A leader whose close was never reached at all (an earlier stop or assessment refused first) is left live and reusable exactly as before.
